A1.justification: Despite the changed title, both PDFs describe RSD and contain matching core methods and experiments. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original RSD generation results on CelebA-HQ and FastMRI, alongside model-selection and efficiency analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original RSD results and adds denoising benchmarks, controlled ablations, synthetic experiments, and conditional reconstruction results.

M1.justification: The core corruption-aware pretraining and SiD distillation procedure remains intact. Limited extensions add calibration-based estimation of unknown noise, sample-dependent noise during distillation, and latent optimization for conditional reconstruction (v2 Section 4.7 and Appendices D.2–D.4).

E1.justification: Beyond v1's CelebA-HQ restoration and FastMRI experiments, v2 adds CIFAR-10, FFHQ, AFHQ-v2, and a synthetic spiral dataset. Coverage expands to explicit denoising, conditional denoising and super-resolution, and heterogeneous or misspecified noise scenarios.

E2.justification: v2 adds comparisons involving SURE-Score, TweedieDiff, SFBD, Teacher-Consistency, clean-data diffusion models, and Rectified Flow. Conditional experiments introduce Noise2Self, DPS-based solvers, and a pseudoinverse baseline; SDS and DMD are now evaluated in a loss ablation. The renamed teacher rows in retained restoration experiments preserve v1's comparators.

E3.justification: New protocols include 10%, 50%, and 100% training-data controls and dataset-specific denoising budgets. Evaluation expands beyond FID to IS, precision, recall, KID, PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS. Conditional evaluations use 250 CIFAR-10 or 100 CelebA-HQ images with specified 1000-step optimization procedures.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's efficiency and Proximal FID analyses, v2 adds data-size, distillation-loss, noise-misspecification, and heterogeneous-noise ablations. Spiral visualizations and precision/recall analyses examine the proposed mechanism and mode coverage. Proximal FID validation also expands to denoising datasets.

E5.justification: v2 adds 95% confidence intervals from 100 noise-estimation trials in Table 14 and ± values for DMD and SiD in Table 18. These are selective additions: Table 18 does not define the uncertainty statistic or run count. v1's explicit generation-seed range is omitted.

E6.justification: The shared CelebA-HQ restoration scores remain unchanged, and MRI scores are only rounded. Substantial new results include CIFAR-10 denoising FID 4.77 at sigma 0.2 (v2 Table 2), conditional super-resolution PSNR 27.803 (Table 16), and numerous ablation results. New timing measurements use different settings and do not establish same-setting speed improvements over v1.

T1.justification: v1's rank-one linear-corruption theorem and proof are retained as v2 Theorem 2. Appendix F adds a rank-r denoising/Wasserstein result, a strict-saddle analysis, variable-noise theory, and assumption-dependent Fisher-divergence bounds incorporating score-estimation and optimization errors, with accompanying proofs.

C1.justification: v1 explicitly presents RSD as extending Denoising Score Distillation beyond denoising. v2 presents a unified framework encompassing denoising and adds contribution-level claims about unknown-noise robustness, data-scale robustness, and conditional inverse solving. The central claim that one-step distillation improves upon corrupted-data teachers remains.

C2.justification: v2 adds a mode-covering versus mode-seeking explanation and distinguishes concentration from mode collapse. It identifies noise underestimation as harmful and qualifies loss rankings because hyperparameters were not tuned. The former conditional-sampling limitation becomes a demonstrated latent-optimization application, while more principled conditioning remains future work.

D1.justification: v2 adds denoising-specific budgets, normalization, dropout, Teacher-Consistency settings, optimizer settings, and an RSD repository URL. Reported hardware changes from A100 to A6000 configurations. Conversely, v1's explicit Gaussian blur kernel specifications and ESPIRiT sensitivity-map calibration details are omitted.

R1.justification: The DSD citation and dedicated comparison appendix disappear, removing v1's explicit predecessor relationship and changing novelty positioning. Citations and discussion expand substantially around SFBD, SURE-Score, Noise2Self, blind denoising, low-dimensional score theory, and scientific inverse problems.

P1.justification: v2 changes the title and extensively rewrites the abstract, introduction, and experimental narrative, adopting consolidated teacher terminology. Theory moves into Appendix F, the RSD algorithm moves into the main text, and the appendices are reorganized with a contents list. Citation style and conference formatting also change.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn to show the corruption pipeline, Table 1 gains objectives and notation, and retained comparison tables are consolidated or rearranged. Numerous denoising, conditional, and ablation tables, toy plots, and image grids are added. The original restoration grids and MRI imagery are retained.

improvement.justification: The new noise-failure, data-size, loss-choice, and mode-coverage analyses address important untested aspects of v1, while conditional reconstruction is demonstrated instead of remaining future work. Expanded theory also goes beyond the original rank-one analysis. Removing explicit DSD positioning and some implementation details weakens transparency, but the added diagnostic evidence and demonstrated applicability provide a substantial net improvement.
